title: The region that went dark
outcome: A standby cluster existed, nobody had rehearsed using it, and a one-hour regional outage became five hours of downtime.

content.bookmark: Cross-cluster replication is asynchronous, so the recovery point is at least the replication lag. A failover that has never been rehearsed is a plan on paper only.

check.prompt: MirrorMaker 2 replicates the topic orders from a cluster aliased primary. What is it called on the standby, by default?
check.why: The default replication policy prefixes the source cluster's alias. Consumers failing over must read the renamed topic.

check.prompt: Besides topic data, what does MirrorMaker 2 replicate?
options: Topic configurations, consumer group offsets and ACLs
check.why: Replicated group offsets let a consumer group resume on the standby near where it stopped.

check.prompt: With asynchronous cross-cluster replication, what is the least data you can expect to lose in a sudden regional failure?
options: Whatever had not yet been replicated: the replication lag at that moment
check.why: Records are copied after they are written to the source, so the most recent ones may not have crossed. Measure the lag and state the RPO honestly.

check.prompt: Which tool keeps the same offsets on the destination as on the source?
options: Confluent Cluster Linking, a Confluent feature rather than part of Apache Kafka
check.why: Cluster Linking mirror topics are byte-for-byte copies with the same offsets. MirrorMaker 2 offsets on the target don't necessarily match the source.

caseStudy.setting: A payments processor (fictional) runs its primary Kafka cluster in one cloud region, with MirrorMaker 2 replicating to a standby cluster in another region. The disaster recovery plan says "fail over to the standby". It has never been tested end to end.

events.what: The primary region has a major network outage. Every service there is unreachable.

Nobody is sure who can declare a disaster. Producers' configs point at the primary's addresses. Consumers expect topic names without the primary. prefix. Credentials for the standby are missing for two services. Each fix is made by hand.
Payments resume on the standby. The primary region had recovered at 10:15. About 30 seconds of payments before the outage never reached the standby.

pipeline: Primary cluster · region A, all producers and consumers
MirrorMaker 2 · primary to standby, topics renamed primary.<name>
DR plan · one line, never rehearsed
tasks: Why did failover take five hours when the outage lasted one?
What should the DR plan have stated?

debrief.title: Why it took so long
text: Every step of failover was being done for the first time: deciding, re-pointing producers, changing consumers to the prefixed topic names, finding credentials.
The standby had the data, but the systems around it weren't ready to use it. By the time they were, the primary was back, and failing back became a second problem.

debrief.title: What could be lost
text: MirrorMaker 2 copies records after they are written to the primary, so the last moments before an outage may never cross. Here, about 30 seconds.
That is the recovery point (RPO) this design really offers. It should be measured from the replication lag and agreed with the business, not discovered.

debrief.title: A plan worth having
text: Stated RPO and RTO per service. Who declares a disaster, and on what signals.
How producers find the standby; how each consumer group resumes, from replicated offsets and on prefixed names; what isn't replicated (schemas, connector configs, credentials).
How to fail back, and a scheduled rehearsal measured against the RPO and RTO.

takeaway: A standby you've never used is not a recovery plan.
Asynchronous replication means RPO is at least the lag.
Rehearse failover and failback, and measure them.
content.honesty: If you haven't run a regional failover, say so and walk through the plan you would write. If you have, lead with what surprised you.

tasks: What would you ask about the DR plan?
What would you require before calling it done?

debrief.title: Questions
text: "How much data could we lose, and how long would we be down?"

debrief.title: Done means
text: RPO and RTO agreed and written; a rehearsal that meets them; repeated on a schedule.

sayIt.question: How would you know a disaster recovery plan actually works?
points: It states RPO and RTO, agreed with the business.
It names who decides and how.
It covers producers, consumers and what isn't replicated.
It has been rehearsed, with results measured.
It is rehearsed again regularly.

tasks: What do you tell merchants and regulators?
How do you decide what RPO and RTO to aim for?

debrief.title: Communication
text: Tell merchants the window and the lost payments; work with them to resubmit. Report to regulators as required.

debrief.title: Targets
text: Set RPO and RTO from what the business can tolerate and what it will pay for; active-passive with asynchronous replication can't promise zero loss.

sayIt.question: How would you set recovery targets for a critical product?
points: Ask what loss and downtime the business can tolerate.
Translate into RPO and RTO.
Show the cost of each level of protection.
Choose an architecture that meets it, honestly stated.
Fund and schedule rehearsals.

tasks: How do you organise the next failover?
How do you make rehearsal routine?

debrief.title: Organising
text: A runbook with steps, owners and timings; a named incident commander with authority to declare.

debrief.title: Routine rehearsal
text: A failover game day each quarter, measured against RPO and RTO, with findings tracked to closure.

sayIt.question: How would you prepare an organisation to fail over a critical system?
points: A runbook with owners and timings.
Clear authority to declare a disaster.
Credentials and configs ready in the standby.
Regular rehearsals, measured.
Track findings to closure.

debrief.title: Technical changes
text: Make topic names and cluster addresses configuration, switchable in one place. Alert on MM2 replication lag and checkpoint-latency-ms.
Replicate or recreate what MM2 doesn't carry: schemas, connector configs, credentials.

debrief.title: MM2 or Cluster Linking
text: MM2 is part of Apache Kafka and runs on Connect; topics are prefixed and offsets differ. Cluster Linking (Confluent only) keeps names and offsets, which simplifies consumer failover, at the cost of a vendor dependency.

sayIt.question: How would you design Kafka for surviving the loss of a region?
points: Replication within a cluster handles brokers and zones; a region needs a second cluster.
MirrorMaker 2 replicates topics, configs, group offsets and ACLs, with prefixed names.
It is asynchronous, so RPO is at least the replication lag.
Plan producer and consumer failover, and what isn't replicated.
Rehearse failover and failback against stated targets.
